acceptance_checks.current_desktop_platform: Electron 42 desktop app in packages/desktop, with @muyajs/core (packages/muya TS rewrite) as the active editor engine
runtime_boundaries_identified: package/process: packages/desktop owns Electron/OS/window/file policy; packages/muya stays a pure editor package without Electron/Node shell; renderer hosts UI, Pinia, and the live editor

security: main process is the authority for native capabilities; renderer has no direct Node access; preload exposes only explicit capabilities (contextIsolation:true, sandbox:true, nodeIntegration:false)

window: BrowserWindow creation/close/active-window and OS open-file routing belong to main; each window keeps its own renderer; BrowserWindow.id must not be treated as a persistent identity (restoreBufferId and renderer tab id are distinct)

file: preserve absolute paths, local file identity, encoding/BOM, LF internal representation, EOL/trailing-newline save semantics, watcher stability window, and atomic durable writes; do not freeze full IFileState, Muya block tree, or history as a cross-layer protocol

editor: Muya is consumed through its public entrypoint; Electron capabilities are injected via callbacks/options; live engine state stays in the renderer; do not yet define a generic multi-engine EditorEngine
IPC/shell: new capabilities use domain-scoped, serializable, sender-bound DTOs; main-internal ipcMain.emit events stay separate from renderer IPC; do not unify everything into one bus

rationale: All load-bearing claims were checked against current sources. Verified: monorepo layout (pnpm-workspace.yaml lists packages/* plus muya examples/e2e); root scripts proxy to desktop (root package.json); security config contextIsolation:true/sandbox:true/nodeIntegration:false/webSecurity:false (config.ts:12-19) with the E2E canary (context-isolation.spec.ts); stale sandbox/layout statements in CLAUDE.md:243-244 and ARCHITECTURE.md, which the answer correctly treated as non-authoritative; WindowManager responsibilities including findBestWindowToOpenIn scoring (windowManager.ts:256) and EditorWindow file-list/watcher ownership (editor.ts:50-146); sidebar file ops through window.fileUtils and ipcRenderer (project.ts:211-270, preload/index.ts:158-180); the intentionally permissive IPC contract (ipc.ts:1-18) mixing renderer and ipcMain.emit channels, with window-file-saved typed [windowId, tabId] (ipc.ts:199) but handled by pathname (windowManager.ts:457); the editor boundary any/shim/synthetic-history state (editor.vue:172,289; muya-core.d.ts:1-18); and atomic durable writes plus load/save semantics (filesystem/index.ts:25-48, markdown.ts:66-158). The parity scoreboard drift is real: the scoreboard claims PG14 is still xfail while the test source is fixed with no test.fail(). Git-history subjects were only partially verifiable in this shell-less environment: c907b29c matches the provided snapshot ('flush pending edits before saving'); the six earlier hashes could not be independently re-derived, but they are supporting context and consistent with the verified current state, so they are not counted as errors. Two minor citation offsets (ipc.ts:183 should be 199; desktop/package.json:55 should be the root package.json) are recorded. No material factual errors. One unresolved decision-relevant documentation/implementation conflict (the parity scoreboard), so the v2.1 gate is mechanically false even though the answer correctly flagged the drift rather than inventing a resolution. All nine dimensions are fully satisfied: the answer classifies the repo from multiple signals, cites exact symbols/paths and separates current evidence from intent, explains where changes spread and why, gives explicit quality-attribute trade-offs with verification, compares three options including the status quo, derives a clear recommendation from drivers and evidence, lays out six incremental/observable/reversible steps, and specifies concrete tests and completion criteria without smuggling project facts into generic rules. Total: 18/18.
